marketInsightsHtml:
La charge de base allemande du 26 décembre a légèrement baissé de 0,85 € à 202,80 €/MWh et la charge de base française a chuté de 3,20 € à 185,00 €/MWh en raison de révisions continentales plus chaudes à court terme, tandis que le 26 décembre britannique a gagné 1,00 £ à 177,75 £/MWh. Le Day-Ahead allemand a plongé de 61,28 € pour s'établir à 146,25 €/MWh alors que l'éolien allemand a grimpé vers 42,6 GW, tandis que le Day-Ahead français est resté stable à 64,24 €/MWh après que le vent ait atteint un record historique de 19,94 GW.

La production éolienne du Royaume-Uni devrait passer de 7,2 GW aujourd'hui à 3,5 GW vendredi et 3,3 GW samedi, tandis que l'éolien français chutera de 16,7 GW aujourd'hui à seulement 5,0 GW samedi et l'éolien allemand reculera de 42,6 GW à 6,6 GW dimanche, soulevant la consommation d'énergie thermique en fin de semaine.

Les fortes pluies alpines et ibériques ont également porté la production française au fil de l'eau à un sommet de 542 GWh en 20 semaines et ont fait grimper les réserves hydroélectriques espagnoles de 330 GWh à 9,9 TWh (capacité de 42,9 %), bien que les stocks hydroélectriques suisses soient tombés à un déficit saisonnier record de 16,4 points de pourcentage en dessous de la normale à 62,3 %.

marketInsights.gas:
European natural gas benchmarks rebounded modestly on Tuesday, recovering a fraction of Monday's losses as fresh Middle East security incidents and unplanned Norwegian maintenance offset mild continental weather.

Dutch TTF front-month gained €0.78 (+0.93%) to settle at €84.46/MWh, while Day-Ahead rose €0.99 (+1.18%) to close at €84.40/MWh. In the UK, NBP Day-Ahead climbed 2.55p (+1.24%) to settle at 208.55p/th, while December 26 added 1.66p (+0.80%) to 210.14p/th. Further out, curve contracts outperformed the prompt on persistent winter supply tightness, with TTF and NBP Q1 2027 settling up at €83.14/MWh and 206.39p/th respectively, while TTF Summer 27 rose to €64.69/MWh.

Upward support was driven by renewed geopolitical friction after the UKMTO confirmed a commercial tanker sustained a second strike in the Strait of Hormuz, alongside reports of Iranian drones targeting a US military radar installation in Bahrain. Reports also warned on Tuesday of a projected 2 million tonne global LNG deficit this winter, even as Qatari shuttle tankers and ADNOC exports continue to navigate the Gulf. Brent crude gave back Tuesday's modest bounce to trade down at $91.76/bbl (-1.48%) this morning, pressured by IEA Q4 surplus expectations and ahead of the upcoming 29 November OPEC+ capacity review.

On the physical supply side, Gassco reported a new unplanned processing outage at Norway’s Troll field taking 10 mcm/day offline, though overall Norwegian planned maintenance continues to tail off through the remainder of November. European storage sits at 70% capacity (down 12 percentage points year-on-year). German facilities are at around 57% full, an 86 TWh deficit to the 2023–25 average, after withdrawing 384 mcm during last week’s cold spell.

While above-normal temperatures across mainland Europe next week have eased fears of an immediate SSW-driven freeze, a cold wedge is pushing down over the UK and Scandinavia through the weekend, with London overnight lows dropping to -1.8°C on Friday and -1.7°C on Saturday.
marketInsights.power:
European power curves posted mixed movements on Tuesday, with forward winter quarters tracking gas higher while prompt contracts diverged sharply.

German December 26 baseload edged down €0.85 to €202.80/MWh and French December fell €3.20 to €185.00/MWh on warmer near-term continental revisions, whereas UK December 26 gained £1.00 to £177.75/MWh. Along the curve, German Q1 2027 rose €4.05 to €188.80/MWh and UK Q1 2027 added £1.25 to £174.00/MWh. Prompt Day-Ahead delivery split dramatically. German Day-Ahead plunged €61.28 to clear at €146.25/MWh as German wind surged toward 42.6 GW, while French Day-Ahead cleared flat at €64.24/MWh after wind hit an all-time record of 19.94 GW. Conversely, UK Day-Ahead climbed £8.37 on N2EX to £185.65/MWh as UK wind began dropping off from Tuesday's peak.

Renewable generation is set to tighten sharply heading into the weekend. UK wind output is forecast to fall from 7.2 GW today down to 3.5 GW on Friday and 3.3 GW on Saturday, while French wind drops from 16.7 GW today to just 5.0 GW by Saturday and German wind retreats from 42.6 GW to 6.6 GW by Sunday, lifting late-week thermal power burn.

Supply margins saw minor relief in Southeast Europe as Bulgaria’s 1 GW Kozloduy Unit 6 completed maintenance two days early and began ramping back to full capacity. Heavy Alpine and Iberian rainfall also lifted French run-of-river output to a 20-week high of 542 GWh and drove Spanish hydro reserves up 330 GWh to 9.9 TWh (42.9% capacity), though Swiss hydro stocks fell to a record seasonal deficit of 16.4 percentage points below normal at 62.3%. Thermal margins saw German December clean spark spreads ease slightly to €13.41/MWh against €83.07/MWh for clean dark spreads, keeping coal firmly in merit ahead of gas.
